adds.title: LGBTQ people in prison (Wikipedia, Canada section)
adds.summary: Wikipedia article (fetched, HTTP 200) covering Canada specifically: after Bill C-16 (2017) prohibited discrimination based on gender identity, transgender prisoners were to be placed in facilities based on their gender identity, with PM Trudeau committing to review assignment so prisoners end up in facilities matching their gender identity, and transgender prisoners to be considered for sex-reassignment surgery if imprisoned more than 12 continuous months. It documents the 31 Aug 2001 Canadian Human Rights Tribunal ruling (Kavanagh) that Sections 30-31 of the Corrections and Conditional Release Act discriminated on grounds of sex and disability after Synthia Kavanagh, a trans woman serving life (sentenced 1989), was assigned to a male institution despite the trial judge's recommendation of a women's facility, was denied hormones and sex-reassignment surgery, and experienced periods of solitude. It also cites a 2022 CTV report alleging a pattern of abuse and discrimination against gender-diverse prisoners in Canadian jails, heightened sexual-assault victimisation, and protective procedures not always followed by staff, plus a 2022 study of Nova Scotia correctional officers (not prisoners).

adds.title: Barbara findlay (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: Wikipedia article (fetched, HTTP 200) recording that Vancouver lawyer barbara findlay represented Synthia Kavanagh, a transgender prisoner, in litigation concerning gender-affirming medical treatment and placement in a women's correctional institution — corroborating the 2001 Canadian Human Rights Tribunal Kavanagh case as Canada's documented trans-prisoner placement litigation (identity-based placement sought against birth-sex assignment).

records.note: Canada's documented practice is gender-identity-based placement embedded in human-rights rulings rather than a trans-specific housing statute: after Bill C-16 (2017) transgender prisoners are to be placed in facilities matching their gender identity (with sex-reassignment surgery consideration for sentences over 12 months) — a shift anchored in the 2001 Canadian Human Rights Tribunal ruling that assigning trans woman Synthia Kavanagh to a male institution (against the sentencing judge's recommendation) and denying hormones/surgery discriminated on sex and disability. Documented trouble remains: a 2022 CTV report alleged gender-diverse prisoners face abuse, discrimination and higher sexual-assault risk in Canadian jails with protection procedures inconsistently followed. No trans special unit was documented; Kavanagh's account references periods of solitude while held in the men's facility.
